title: Polynomial-Time Block Membership Test
statement: Let $V$ be a language of finite bit strings whose Boolean membership indicator, output as a one-bit word, is polynomial-time computable. For any $a,k,a',k'\in\mathbb{N}$, the following function is polynomial-time computable: on input $z$, let $x$ and $y$ be the first and second components obtained by parsing $z$ as a pair (using the empty word for a component when parsing fails); divide $y$ into consecutive blocks of length $a(|x|+1)^k$, starting at its beginning, and form the one-bit output that is true exactly when at least one of the first $a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$ such blocks, paired with $x$, belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of finite bit strings
The one-bit membership indicator of $V$ is polynomial-time computable
